title: 10.7 · Nodal analysis
question: Find the node voltage V.

steps.title: Write KCL
steps.body: Current entering from the left equals the three currents leaving the node.

steps.title: Collect the V terms
steps.body: Move the current source to the left and factor V on the right.

steps.title: Divide in rectangular form
steps.body: Use rectangular form when adding or subtracting complex numbers.

steps.title: Convert to polar form
steps.body: Find the magnitude and angle. Both parts are negative, so V is in the third quadrant.

check: Substituting this voltage into KCL balances the entering and leaving currents.

title: 10.25 · Mesh analysis
question: Find the downward capacitor current iₒ(t).

steps.title: Convert to phasors
steps.body: Use cosine as the reference. The sine source has a −90° phase shift.

steps.title: Write the mesh equations
steps.body: Choose clockwise mesh currents I₁ on the left and I₂ on the right. Their currents oppose each other in the capacitor.

steps.title: Solve for the two currents
steps.body: Divide the first equation by 2 and the second by j2. Substitute I₂ = 3 − I₁ into the first.

steps.title: Find the shared current
steps.body: Downward capacitor current is the left mesh current minus the right mesh current.

check: The mesh currents satisfy both equations; their difference gives the marked downward current.

title: 10.40 · Superposition
question: Find the downward inductor current iₒ(t).

steps.title: Keep only the DC source
steps.body: Short the AC voltage source. At DC steady state, the inductor is a short circuit.

steps.title: Keep only the AC source
steps.body: Short the 8 V source. At ω = 4 rad/s, the inductor impedance is j4 Ω.

steps.title: Transform the AC source
steps.body: The 10 V source with 4 Ω in series becomes a 2.5 A source with 4 Ω in parallel. Combine the two parallel resistors.

steps.title: Use current division
steps.body: Find the current in the inductor branch.

steps.title: Add in the time domain
steps.body: Add the constant DC current to the AC waveform.

check: The average current is 4 A. The AC part has zero average; different frequencies are added in the time domain.

title: 10.49 · Source transformation
question: Find i(t) in the right-hand branch.

steps.title: Find the impedances
steps.body: Keep a sine reference for this question, so the source is 8∠30° A.

steps.title: Transform the source
steps.body: Replace the current source and parallel 5 Ω resistor with a voltage source and series 5 Ω resistor.

steps.title: Add the series impedances
steps.body: The transformed circuit is one series loop.

steps.title: Divide voltage by impedance
steps.body: Divide magnitudes and subtract angles.

check: The negative impedance angle means current leads the source. Keep the sine reference in the final answer.

title: 10.55(a) · Thevenin and Norton
question: Find both equivalent circuits at terminals a–b.

steps.title: Find the equivalent impedance
steps.body: Turn off the independent voltage source by shorting it. The 10 Ω resistor is in series with the parallel reactances.

steps.title: Find the open-circuit voltage
steps.body: With a–b open, no current flows through 10 Ω. The terminal voltage is the capacitor voltage.

steps.title: Find the Norton current
steps.body: Divide the open-circuit voltage by the equivalent impedance.

check: Thevenin: voltage source in series with Zth. Norton: current source in parallel with ZN. Use + at a and a Norton source arrow from b to a.

title: 10.55(b) · Thevenin and Norton
question: Find both equivalent circuits at terminals a–b.

steps.title: Find the equivalent impedance
steps.body: Turn off the independent current source by opening it. Looking into a–b, j10 Ω is in parallel with 8 − j5 Ω.

steps.title: Find the inductor current
steps.body: Restore the source and leave a–b open. Use current division between 8 Ω and the series branch −j5 + j10.

steps.title: Find the open-circuit voltage
steps.body: The voltage at a–b is across the j10 Ω inductor.

steps.title: Find the Norton current
steps.body: Divide magnitudes and subtract angles.

check: Thevenin: Vth in series with Zth. Norton: IN in parallel with ZN. Use + at a and a Norton source arrow from b to a.
